source.title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces

accepted.question_text: Let X be an F-space equipped with an F-norm ||x||. Must there always exist an equivalent F-norm on X such that for every nonzero x, the function t ↦ ||tx|| for positive t is analytic?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 1. - Let X be an F-space with a norm || x|| . Does always an equivalent analytic norm exist ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an F-space. Does X always contain an infinite-dimensional subspace that admits an equivalent unbounded F-norm, where an F-norm ||x||' is called unbounded when sup_{x in X} ||x||' = +∞? Also, does there exist a subspace M of X such that the quotient space X/M admits an unbounded F-norm?
accepted.context_brief: Unbounded norms on subspaces and quotients

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 2. - Does each F-space contains -an infinite dimensional subspace with unbounded norm ? Does there exist a subspace such that in the quotient space there is an unbounded norm ?

accepted.question_text: Let X and Y be F-spaces, possibly with nonhomogeneous F-norms, and let U: X -> Y be a rotation, meaning an isometry with U(0) = 0. Must every such rotation be a linear operator?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 3. - Is each rotation a linear operator ?

accepted.question_text: If X and Y are locally bounded F-spaces and U: X -> Y is a rotation, meaning an isometry with U(0) = 0, must U be linear even without assuming that the F-norms are concave?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 3T• - Is each rotation mapping a locally bounded space onto a locally bounded space linear without the assumption of concavity of norms ?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a separable Banach space admits a transitive norm, meaning that for any two norm-one vectors x and y there is an isometry sending x to y. Must that Banach space be a Hilbert space?

evidence.quote: There is an old question of Banach : does each separable Banach space with transitive norm is a Hilbert space ? The answer is not known

accepted.question_text: Consider the Banach space C[0,1] of continuous real-valued functions on the interval [0,1] with the supremum norm. Is this supremum norm maximal, meaning that whenever an equivalent F-norm has a larger group of rotations, the two groups of rotations must in fact coincide?
accepted.context_brief: Maximality of sup norm on C[0,1]

evidence.quote: PROBLEM U. - Is the norm sup in the space C[0, 1] of continuous real on interval [0, 1] maximal ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an F-space with F-norm ||x|| and rotation group G(||.||). Does there exist a Banach space Y with a homogeneous norm whose rotation group is exactly G(||.||)?
accepted.context_brief: Realizing rotation groups in Banach spaces

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 5. - Let X be an F-space with an F-norm [[x || . Does a Banach space Y with a homogeneous norm || x |j such that G( || |[) = G( |[ || ) exist ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an F-space, let Ω be a measurable space with sigma-field Σ, and let μ: Σ -> X be a nonatomic countably additive X-valued measure. For every bounded measurable scalar-valued function x(t), must the integral ∫_Ω x(t) dμ(t) exist?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 6. - Suppose that p(E) is nonatomic. Does exists an integral J x(t) dp(t) for each measurable bounded, scalar valued function x(t) ?

accepted.question_text: Let X = S[0,1], the space of all measurable functions on [0,1] endowed with convergence in measure. For every X-valued countably additive measure μ and every bounded measurable scalar-valued function x(t), must the integral ∫ x(t) dμ exist?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 7. - Let X = S[0, I], Does an integral f x(t) dp exist for each measu-rable "bounded scalar valued function x(t) and each measure p(E) ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a nuclear F-space in the sense defined via diametral approximative dimension. Is every unconditionally convergent series in X necessarily absolutely convergent?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 8. - Let X be a nuclear F-space. Does each unconditionally convergent series is absolutely convergent ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a nuclear F-space that is locally pseudo-convex but not locally convex?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 9* - Does a nuclear locally pseudo-convex non-locally convex F-space exist ?
After the Conference J.P. Ligaud has shown that each nuclear locally pseudo-convex space is locally convex

accepted.question_text: In every nuclear F-space, must there exist a nontrivial continuous linear functional?
accepted.context_brief: Continuous linear functionals on nuclear F-spaces

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 10. - Do in each nuclear F-space non trivial linear continuous functionals exist ?

accepted.question_text: Must every infinite-dimensional F-space that is not locally bounded contain an infinite-dimensional nuclear subspace?
accepted.context_brief: Nuclear subspaces in non-locally bounded F-spaces

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 11. - Does each non-locally bounded infinite dimensional F-space contain an infinite dimensional nuclear space ?

accepted.question_text: Is every nuclear F-space a Montel space, meaning that every bounded subset is compact?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 12. - Is each nuclear space a Montel space ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an F-space and K a bounded subset of X. Suppose that for every open starlike set U containing 0 as an internal point, the diametral approximative quantities δ_n(K,U) tend to 0 as n -> ∞. Must K be compact?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 12T. - Let X be an F-space. Let K be a bounded set. Suppose that for each open starlike U containing 0 as an internal point 5^(K, U) ^ 0 . Is K a compact set ?

accepted.question_text: Does every infinite-dimensional F-space contain an infinite-dimensional F-subspace that has nontrivial continuous linear functionals? Does this remain true under the additional assumptions that the ambient space is locally bounded, or nuclear, or has no unbounded norms?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM lU. - Does each infinite dimensional F-space contains an infinite dimen-sional F-subspace with nontrivial linear continuous functionals ? Does it hold if we additionally assume that the space is either locally bounded or nuclear or without unbounded norms ?

accepted.question_text: If an F-space has no unbounded norm, must it contain a copy of the sequence space s of all scalar sequences?
accepted.context_brief: Spaces without unbounded norms and copies of s

evidence.quote: It is not known does each space without unbounded norm contains the space s .

accepted.question_text: Does every F-space contain a subspace M such that the quotient space X/M has nontrivial continuous linear functionals?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 15. - Does each F-space contain a subspace such that there are nontrivial linear continuous functionals in the quotient space ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a non-locally convex F-space. Does X contain a subspace M such that the quotient space X/M has no nontrivial continuous linear functionals?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM l6 • - Let X be a non-locally convex space. Does X contain a subspace such that there is no nontrivial linear continuous functionals in the quotient space ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an F-space with no nontrivial continuous linear functionals, and let x_1 be any element of X. Must there exist a continuously differentiable path x:[0,1] -> X with x(0)=0, x(1)=x_1, and vanishing derivative x'(t)=0 for all t?
accepted.context_brief: Paths with zero derivative in F-spaces

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 17. - Let X be an F-space without nontrivial linear continuous func-tional. Let x-€ X . Does a function x(t) with vanishing derivative such that x(o) = 0 and x(l) = x exist ?
